solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush mats coming back deep woven

indicators.note: coming back means the word mats is read from its end to its start
woven means the letters of deep are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hurries some mats along while weaving a deep pattern into them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns MATS into STAM, and 'woven' rearranges DEEP into PEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden mass charge of animals or people is a frantic rush, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Very little food served in a tureen — swindle

parts.note: a tureen is a deep dish for serving soup
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A guest feels cheated by the tiny portion of soup ladled from the tureen.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a French borrowing meaning a tiny trace or hint, such as a touch of garlic.

clue.text: Legitimate banning learner driver that's very bad

indicators.note: banning means the learner letter is excluded from the word for legitimate

parts.note: legitimate means lawful
L is the learner plate shown by British learner drivers

explanation.surface: A legal ban on learner drivers is condemned as terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banning' removes L from LAWFUL. British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or terrible is extremely poor in quality, the everyday intensified sense.

clue.text: Left is holding thinning out operation which blocks entrants

indicators.note: holding says the left side and is together wrap round the culling word

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a cull reduces an animal population by selective killing

explanation.surface: A sentence about a left-hand gate being part of a culling programme that keeps people out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left is' reads as a sentence opening, but port (the left side of a ship) and the word is are what does the 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the heavy grille lowered at a castle gateway to stop anyone getting in.

clue.text: Depressing hearing organ in Derby in odd places

indicators.note: in says the hearing organ goes inside the letters picked from Derby
in odd places means take the first, third and fifth letters of Derby

parts.note: the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A sad tale of an ear found somewhere odd in Derby, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in odd places' picks D, R and Y from Derby; 'in' puts EAR among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and gloomy is cheerless and lowers the spirits.

clue.text: Cry out when there's no oxygen close

indicators.note: there's no signals that the oxygen letter is absent from the shouting word

parts.note: to cry out is to shout
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Someone yells when a room runs out of air to breathe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no' removes O from SHOUT. 'Close' reads as an adjective or a sound but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To close a door or lid is to shut it: a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Disliking importing energy — something needed in winter

indicators.note: importing means bringing the energy letter inside the word for disliking

parts.note: disliking intensely is hating
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone resents paying for imported energy, which is needed in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Warming homes in the cold months is a requirement, so the definition describes it loosely.

clue.text: Meeting of lovers in country station

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words country station

explanation.surface: Two lovers arrange to meet at a rural railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across countRY STation.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret romantic appointment between lovers is a rendezvous.

clue.text: One leaving uniform edition not fully developed

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for one departs from the word uniform

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A soldier quits, leaving the uniform edition of some publication half-finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes I out of UNIFORM to give UNFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still without its final shape is immature, lacking its finished structure.

clue.text: Cautious of danger of route across river

indicators.note: across says the route stretches over, so encloses, the river letter

parts.note: a way is a route
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of the dangers of a road that crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on guard against harm is the core sense of being watchful and careful.

clue.text: Handling crew a long time before people start to travel

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
an age is a long time
men are people

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of travel is used

explanation.surface: A tour company crew spends ages before people can set off on their trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Running or controlling a business or situation is the act of handling it.

clue.text: Stomach upset from endless cold ice

indicators.note: endless means each of the two words loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone blames a tummy ache on swallowing very cold ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes D from cold and E from ice, leaving COL and IC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an attack of abdominal pain, common in babies and horses, so it is a stomach upset.

clue.text: One with no illusions about a catalogue

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a catalogue is a list

explanation.surface: A clear-eyed person comments on a sales catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist sees things as they actually are, so has no illusions.

clue.text: Common weed bug

definitions.meaning: a stinging plant found everywhere in hedgerows
to bug someone is to irritate or annoy them

explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a familiar stinging weed, and as a verb it means to irritate, just as bugging does.

clue.text: Severe weather is too darn bad

indicators.note: bad signals that the letters of too darn are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a storm is just too darn bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is an extreme weather event.

clue.text: Inhibition how to end a phone call

definitions.text: how to end a phone call
definitions.meaning: you put the receiver down, hanging up, to finish a call

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a nagging inhibition; as a phrasal verb it is replacing the receiver to finish a call.

clue.text: Talk quickly with new example to be followed

parts.note: patter is fast, glib talk, as of a salesman

explanation.surface: A fast talker sets a new example for others to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A model or template is something to copy, such as a dressmaker's guide.

clue.text: Very much want European father to support daughter

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting letters sit below, so the European father goes under the daughter letter

parts.note: to sire is to father, and a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A European father is keen to support his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'to support' puts E + SIRE below D.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to long for or crave something strongly.

clue.text: A diner's ordered fish

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a fresh sequence, playing on ordering food

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer has ordered a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like the diner choosing from the menu, but it rearranges the letters of A DINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: This small oily fish of the herring family is often sold tinned.

clue.text: Sailing boat needs only small areas of water to turn

indicators.note: to turn means the word for small areas of water is read backwards, upward in this down answer

parts.note: pools are small areas of water

explanation.surface: A yacht needs only a little water to turn round in.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a single-masted sailing vessel, a type of sailing boat.

clue.text: English might, needing to lose mass for racing boat

indicators.note: needing to lose says the mass letter must be dropped from the word might

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: English rowing power must be trimmed down to suit a lightweight racing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing to lose' takes M from MIGHT, leaving IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing shell crewed by that many oarsmen, as in the Boat Race, is called by the number.

clue.text: Travelling right away from Goring

indicators.note: away from says the right letter is taken out of the place name

explanation.surface: Someone is travelling on the right, away from Goring, a village on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes R from GORING; Goring is a riverside village in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the move or on one's way is the progressive sense of this verb form.

clue.text: Certainly, old girl

parts.note: Kay is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone agrees cheerfully, addressing a friend as old girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words of assent: saying yes, all right, sure.

clue.text: Be partial to sage just the same

parts.note: to be partial to something is to like it
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of the herb sage, and feels the same way about others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' reads as the herb but is the adjective meaning wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in the same way or also, as in replying 'and you too'.

clue.text: In favour of Mahler's First for concert

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: First here means only the opening letter of the composer's name is used, punning on a First Symphony

explanation.surface: Someone backs programming Mahler's First Symphony at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like the title of Mahler's Symphony No 1 but takes only the M. The Proms are London's famous summer classical concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for promenade concert, where much of the audience stands, as at the BBC Proms.

clue.text: SHAPE military headquarters

definitions.meaning: a five-sided figure is a geometrical shape; printed in capitals because SHAPE is also the acronym of NATO's European headquarters
the US Department of Defense building in Virginia

explanation.definitionFit: It is a five-sided polygon and also the name of the US defence headquarters, which is built in that form.
